page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance hosted on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7T83 processor running at 2.55 GHz, it provides 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. System memory comprises 64.0 GB of RAM, resulting in a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The instance features no local attached storage and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps without integrated GPUs.

Performance benchmarks show strong single-core CPU throughput, evaluated in top-tier results for single-threaded stress testing. The platform delivers strong scores in memory performance and small-model LLM text generation. However, multi-core CPU scaling and general integer compute fall within average ranges. Large-block uncached memory write operations show relative weakness compared to read performance.

Due to its compute-dense configuration with a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, ecs.c7a.8xlarge provides qualitative cost efficiency for CPU-bound tasks that do not require high memory density or bundled storage. It is suitable for batch processing, web serving, software compilation, medium-scale machine learning inference, and microservices workloads reliant on remote network storage.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance equipped with 32 dedicated vCPUs from an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7T83 processor operating at 2.55 GHz and 64.0 GB of RAM. Running on KVM hypervisors, it maintains a 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio without local storage or GPU accelerators. Network baseline throughput is rated at 8 Gbps. Benchmarks highlight strong single-core CPU capability, high PassMark memory scores, and strong text generation speeds on small language models, while multi-core processing and large memory write operations demonstrate average to weak relative throughput. The absence of local disk drives requires reliance on cloud network volumes. This instance offers solid cost efficiency for CPU-intensive parallel operations, software compilation, code build pipelines, microservices, and static web serving workloads that require focused processing power without massive memory overhead.
